title: NUSA Aves: Passive Bioacoustic Monitoring for Endangered Birds
summary: The bird classification research turned into something a conservation officer can actually run. Finalist at BRIN AIDeaNation 2026, 1 of 80 teams selected nationally.
highlights: Team leader and AI engineer: built the model, backend, and CLI/API.
Dockerised inference service with CI/CD, released at v1.0.0, wrapping the fine-tuned BirdNET pipeline for field use.
Reference data for all 219 species covering descriptions, images, and conservation status, served to a Flutter mobile client.
Selected as 1 of 80 finalist teams nationally out of the BRIN AIDeaNation 2026 proposal round.

title: Bone Metastasis Diagnosis Framework
summary: Open-source bone scan diagnosis pipeline. Patient-level AUC 0.956, above EXINI and BONENAVI, both commercial systems used in clinics today.
highlights: Hotspot detection with YOLOv8. mAP@0.5 = 0.599.
Skeletal segmentation with nnU-Net v2 across 12 anatomical regions. IoU 0.879.
Patient-level classification with XGBoost and LightGBM. AUC 0.956; BSI correlated with clinical burden at r = 0.82.
Surpasses commercially deployed EXINI (0.83–0.88) and BONENAVI (0.84–0.89).
narrative: Staging bone metastasis requires computing a Bone Scan Index from whole-body scintigraphy images, a task currently done by two proprietary commercial systems with no open alternative. This project built a fully open pipeline: annotating scans from scratch under physician supervision, training detection and segmentation models, and quantifying BSI automatically. The goal was clinical-grade accuracy with complete transparency.

title: Driver Behaviour Analysis and Fatigue Detection System
summary: Mining fleet dashcams. Real drivers. An 11% F1 gain over the company's existing model. Running in production.
highlights: Extracted facial landmark sequences per frame covering eye closure, mouth movement, and head orientation.
Facial landmark sequence model trained on real dashcam footage. Test accuracy 0.85.
Async cloud-review API: immediate response, background inference pipeline, automatic result delivery to Trans Track.
Live polling runner fetches alarm events and writes verdicts to structured Excel reports.
Full test suite covering unit, pipeline, and live integration tests against the production MDVR server.
Deployed in a Docker-containerised environment. Live demo on Streamlit Cloud.
narrative: Trans Track needed a fatigue detection model that could outperform the system already running on their mining fleet dashcams. Starting from real footage from three active fleets, not synthetic data, made this harder than typical benchmark work. The constraint: beat a production baseline and deploy to live infrastructure.

title: Deep Learning for Bird Sound Identification
summary: 219 bird species. 17 Borneo endemics. 18 IUCN-threatened. Trained on jungle recordings, tested at Bandung Zoo and Malaysia National Zoo.
highlights: Fine-tuned BirdNET v2.4 with MixIT source separation across 12,511 recordings and 219 species.
Endemic/endangered subset: accuracy 0.661, macro F1 0.419.
Full test set: accuracy 0.72, macro F1 0.554, weighted F1 0.724.
Dataset from Xeno-canto and PBHAR, including 8,840 negative samples, split by recording to prevent leakage.
narrative: Passive acoustic monitoring is one of the most cost-effective ways to track bird populations across large conservation areas in Southeast Asia. No existing model was trained on the endemic and endangered species of Indonesia, Malaysia, and Borneo. This project built the dataset from scratch, adapted an established model to the regional subset, and validated it in real zoo environments with no controlled conditions.

title: Telrax: Multi-Task Chest X-Ray Analysis Platform
summary: Five AI modules in one CXR system: classification, organ segmentation, report generation, VQA, visual grounding. Ships as both a web app and a desktop app.
highlights: Pathology classification across 14 disease categories, expanding to 20+ aligned to Indonesian Ministry of Health categories. Fine-tuned on VinBig and NIH ChestX-ray14, comparing DenseNet and transformer-based architectures.
Organ segmentation covering right lung, left lung, and heart, outputting masks and annotated overlays from DICOM inputs.
Report generation producing structured clinical findings and impressions from CXR images.
Backend: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker Compose; AI modules served as microservices.
Interactive report editor with doctor-editable findings, probability bars, and canvas annotation tools.
narrative: Reading a chest X-ray involves multiple simultaneous tasks: identifying pathologies, locating organs, generating a structured report, and answering clinical questions. This project builds a five-module platform where each task is a separate AI module, delivered together as a unified clinical tool for radiologist-assisted diagnosis.

title: Provider-Aware Contrastive Learning for B2B Travel Inventory
summary: Four providers, 3.69 million accommodation records, and a five-star rating that means something different depending on who sent it. Contrastive embeddings raise cross-provider neighbour mixing from 16.7% to 59.1%. 1st Winner, ICoICT 2026 Challenge.
highlights: Trained a contrastive encoder on 3,686,694 records from RateHawk, Expedia, Agoda, and HotelBeds using NT-Xent loss, with positive pairs drawn from destination and quality-tier co-membership.
Stochastic provider-token masking during training, token always masked at inference. 128-dimensional embeddings from a 204,248-parameter encoder.

Introduced CP-NN@K, a cross-provider nearest-neighbour mixing protocol for settings with no verified property links. CP-NN@10 rises from 16.7% to 59.1% and mean per-dimension KS divergence falls from 0.304 to 0.130.
Beat every alignment baseline tested: CORAL 57.9%, MMD 58.2%, gradient reversal 58.4%, provider-token removal 57.9%. None improved on plain stochastic masking.
Reported honestly as a representation result. Provider identity stays partially recoverable (classifier AUC 0.957 to 0.775) and 59.1% remains 15.9 points under the 75.0% random-mixing ceiling.
narrative: B2B travel platforms resell the same hotel through several providers, and each provider grades quality on its own scale. The worst-separated pair of star-rating distributions in the Travlr data differ by a KS divergence of 0.707, and one provider supplies 53.7% of inventory against 6.4% of bookings. With no verified links between listings of the same physical property, this trains on a weaker signal, destination and tier co-membership, and measures success by how well providers mix in the neighbourhood of each property.

title: VLM-Based Chest X-Ray Anomaly Explanation
summary: Grad-CAM tells you where the model looked. This system tells you what it found, in words a radiologist can actually use.
highlights: Three-module pipeline: anomaly detection, visual-text alignment, and structured clinical report generation.
Explanation quality evaluated directly by radiologists on a 100-case gold-standard subset, not only BLEU or BERTScore.
Target: external clinical validation and integration into radiology reporting workflows.

title: Telplastina: WBBS Diagnostic Application
summary: Full-stack diagnostic application for whole-body bone scintigraphy analysis, integrating the bone segmentation, hotspot detection, and BSI quantification pipeline into a deployable clinical tool.
highlights: Integrates bone segmentation and hotspot detection pipelines into a unified clinical web application.
Backend in Rust for high-performance image processing and inference serving.
Frontend in Vue 3 with Docker containerisation for clinical deployment.

title: Gated Mixture-of-Experts Fusion for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
institution: Telkom University · AI Lab Focused Group
summary: Every segment reports which modality caught the fake. Audio-video forgeries route to the audio expert (α 0.178), video-only forgeries to the visual expert (α 0.880). Runs at 5x real time on a 6GB laptop GPU. Accepted at ICoDSA 2026.
highlights: A Modality Reliability Gate routes each 2-second segment to an audio or visual expert using two learned anomaly scores: cross-modal attention residual and VideoMAE temporal variance.
The gate emits a scalar α per segment naming which modality drove the verdict. No compared method (FTCN, LAA-Net, CADDM, CAD) produces this signal.
F1 0.9076, AUC 0.9744, AP 0.9948 on the combined five-dataset split. Static concatenation edges it at F1 0.9096, so the gain here is interpretability, not accuracy.
Across five leave-one-dataset-out runs, AP holds (up to 0.9992) but fixed-threshold F1 drops to 0.585 mean. Ranking survives domain shift, the decision threshold does not.
223,445 segments from PolyglotFake, FakeAVCeleb, HiDF, CelebDFv2, and FF++, split at subject level.
404.7 ms per 2-second window on an RTX 4050 Laptop: a 2-minute video analysed in 24 seconds.
narrative: Most audio-visual detectors assume both channels are equally corrupted. They break when only one is: a face-swapped video with genuine audio, or synthesised speech over real footage. This project built a gate that decides per segment which modality to trust, and reports that decision as a number a forensic analyst can read. The accuracy matches static fusion rather than beating it; what static fusion cannot do is tell you why it decided.

title: Sentiment Analysis Classification: Multi-Class Text
summary: Multi-class text sentiment classifier (positive, neutral, negative) built as a final project for the CCI Data Research Division.
highlights: Compared LSTM, GRU, BERT, LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost on the same dataset.
Achieved 70% accuracy, improved iteratively through embedding and architecture experiments.

title: Retogen: Article Management Platform
summary: Full-stack web platform for publishing and moderating tech-review articles, built as a production-grade system with complete test coverage.
highlights: JWT authentication with user and admin roles; full article lifecycle including image upload with format validation.
Hierarchical nested comments and 1–5 star ratings.
185 automated tests covering authentication, CRUD operations, and edge cases.

title: Anothem: Desktop AI Storytelling Engine
summary: Local LLM desktop application for AI-assisted creative writing, designed to run entirely on consumer hardware with no cloud dependency.
highlights: Runs multiple local LLMs, including a custom recurrent model, entirely on consumer hardware with no cloud required.
Token-streamed UI with background incremental summarization to maintain context across long writing sessions.
Auto-detects narrative intent (description, dialogue, scene) and injects appropriate writing guidance per generation.

title: Real-Time AR Face Filter App
summary: Browser-based augmented reality app demonstrating live face-tracking overlays, developed to increase engagement for a local UMKM churos business.
highlights: Runs at 10 FPS on Streamlit Cloud with no local installation: face detection and 3 animated overlays.
WebRTC live video with server-side overlay compositing applied per frame.
Pure OpenCV pipeline for zero native library dependencies on Streamlit Cloud.
